slides.title: 3 holiday jobs and what they pay
slides.sub: Ranked by median hourly pay (BLS, May 2025). None of them needs a degree.

slides.heading: #1 Stocker
body: Stockers move products from the stockroom to the shelves, or pick and pack customer orders in a warehouse.
You learn on the job, usually in a month or less. Expect to be on your feet and lifting boxes.

slides.heading: #2 Retail salesperson
body: You help customers find what they need, answer questions and often run the register.
Training happens on the job and usually lasts a few days to a few months. No diploma is required.

slides.heading: #3 Cashier
body: Cashiers ring up purchases and handle payments. There's no formal education requirement.
Training may take a few weeks. Ask about employee discounts and holiday shift pay before you accept.

slides.heading: Median hourly pay
slides.note: Stocker pay is the yearly median divided by 2,080 hours

slides.takeaway: Before you say yes, check the pay, the schedule and whether the job ends in January.

posts.caption:
Need holiday cash? These 3 jobs hire a lot of seasonal workers and don't need a degree. Pay is the national median hourly wage from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (May 2025), so half of workers earn more and half earn less.

1. Stocker and order filler: about $17.95 an hour ($37,330 a year median). You move products to shelves or pack orders, and training usually takes a month or less.
2. Retail salesperson: $17.03 an hour. You help customers and run the register, with training that lasts a few days to a few months.
3. Cashier: $15.81 an hour. You ring up purchases and handle payments, with training that may take a few weeks.

All three pay more than double the $7.25 federal minimum wage. Pay varies a lot by state and store, so compare offers.

Pay data: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook (May 2025 wages). Ranked by Claude by median pay.
